- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and prices are rising, model often fails to capture early reversal; adjust downward bias early in upward trends.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day averages when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply a “mean reversion” correction: cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows a recent 0.50 (e.g., 2022-12-01), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to “late correction” bias — true values often dip after day 15–20; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day after day 15.
